name: Lugbara
region: West Nile, Uganda (Arua, Maracha, Terego, Yumbe) and north-eastern DR Congo
translator_note: Written in everyday Arua Lugbara addressed to one person (mi), with the affirmative ra, the perfective 'bo, the negative ku, the -zu purpose nominal (pimazu = for measuring, a price estimate) and the implosive apostrophes of the standard orthography ('ba, 'du, 'yo, e'yo). Buttons are bare verbs: Tu (board), Awa (share), Kodi (rent), Pe (send), 'Du UG si (take it on UG). Concepts with no settled Lugbara word use the loans heard in Arua town (motoka, siteji, simu, sende, bei, app, link, kodi, sandbox, plug-in). No native reviewer has read this: word order in the longer sentences, the choice of 'du for both drive and book, and eco for choose are the weakest points, and every paragraph is a close paraphrase.
